parts.t: The vast majority of BC poultry production sits in one short stretch of the Fraser Valley, and the operating farms below, broiler, turkey and layer operations across Abbotsford, Chilliwack and Langley, are how buyers get in. With the new entrant program currently closed, buying an existing farm or quota is effectively the only route into commercial poultry in BC. Call or text Jared Gibbons at 604-928-1361 for off-market farms and confidential evaluations.

Poultry farms are among the most specialized real estate transactions in BC — the supply-managed quota can be worth as much as the land and barns. Here’s an overview of how the market works and where to look by sector and region.

How does poultry quota work when buying a farm?

Quota is the right to produce a set volume, and it typically carries much of a farm’s value. Quota does not simply run with the land. Any transfer must be applied for by both parties and approved by the applicable marketing board, and it isn’t included in a sale unless expressly stated in the Contract of Purchase and Sale.
